claim: For every \(\beta\in[0,3]\), let \(X_\beta=(\mathbb R^2,N_\beta)\) with \(N_\beta(x,y)=(x^4+2\beta x^2y^2+y^4)^{1/4}\). Then the exact Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance is \[d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_\beta,\ell_2^2)=\begin{cases}(2/(1+\beta))^{1/4},&0\le\beta\le1,\\((1+\beta)/2)^{1/4},&1\le\beta\le3.\end{cases}\] Equivalently, \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_\beta,\ell_2^2)^4=\max\{2/(1+\beta),(1+\beta)/2\}\), and the standard Euclidean norm is an optimal Euclidean pullback; any positive rescaling has the same distortion. The defining norm is invariant under the symmetries of \(N_\beta\).
integrity: The proof is analytic and exact. The bundled exact-arithmetic replay is supplementary and is not used as a substitute for the global group-averaging proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is only for the real two-dimensional quartic family classified by the cited source. It does not classify all optimal linear maps or nonsymmetric cubic-index-zero norms. An older equivalent convex-geometric formulation remains a residual bibliographic risk.
title: Exact Euclidean Banach--Mazur profile of the quartic polynomial-index-zero plane family
